hypotheses.reasoning: notif-db reports at 15:58:45 that transaction 83136, owned by template-svc-reconciler, has been ACTIVE for 90s while holding a row lock on notifications. The lock is never released, so from 15:59:30 onward notif-db returns 'Lock wait timeout' on UPDATE notifications (#3550, #3598, #3733). template-svc's UPDATEs on notifications then hit the 10s limit and statement_timeout (#3568, #3751, #3819). notification-svc's render calls to template-svc time out at 15s (#3577, #3760, #3829). That saturates the template-svc connection pool (#3890, #3988, #4069) and causes pool checkout timeouts (#4223). The result is the gateway 504s on POST /v1/notify (#3914, #4038, #4231). The pool, 504 and retry lines are downstream impact and are not cited as origin evidence. Ruled out: the geo-IP 503s and circuit breaker (enrichment-svc) only affect /v1/events and ingest. The billing-reconciler checksum errors (#1722 onward) are a separate archive-partition problem with no link to the notify path. The notif-worker v3.2.0 rollout at 15:57:45 (#3217) came after the lock holder's transaction had already started (about 15:57:15), and notif-worker logged no errors, so it is an unlikely trigger, though I could not confirm why the reconciler transaction was left open.

The notif-worker v3.2.0 rollout at 15:57:45 is close to the onset of the lock contention. However, the lock holder started about 30s before the deploy and notif-worker shows no errors afterwards, so the link is unconfirmed. Would be the cause if the reconciler's open transaction was introduced by the new build.

verdict.recommendedAction: Identify and kill the stuck template-svc-reconciler transaction (83136) on notif-db so the row lock is released, then verify notif-db lock waits clear. Investigate why the reconciler left a transaction open for 90s+ (check whether it runs with autocommit off or holds the transaction across a slow external call), and add a lock/idle-transaction timeout. Review whether the notif-worker v3.2.0 rollout (build 86be658) changed the reconciler's behaviour. Consider a circuit breaker or shorter timeout on notification-svc to template-svc so the pool does not saturate. Separately, follow up on the billing-reconciler checksum errors in invoice_archive 2019 partitions and the geo-IP provider 503s, which are out of scope for this incident.

hypotheses.reasoning: notif-db reports at 15:58:45 that transaction 83136, owned by template-svc-reconciler, has been ACTIVE for 90s while holding a row lock on notifications. The lock is never released, so from 15:59:30 onward notif-db returns 'Lock wait timeout' on UPDATE notifications (#3550, #3598, #3733). template-svc's UPDATEs on notifications then hit the 10s limit and statement_timeout (#3568, #3751, #3819). notification-svc's render calls to template-svc time out at 15s (#3577, #3760, #3829). That saturates the template-svc connection pool (#3890, #3988, #4069) and causes pool checkout timeouts (#4223). The result is the gateway 504s on POST /v1/notify (#3914, #4038, #4231). The pool, 504 and retry lines are downstream impact and are not cited as origin evidence. Ruled out: the geo-IP 503s and circuit breaker (enrichment-svc) only affect /v1/events and ingest. The billing-reconciler checksum errors (#1722 onward) are a separate archive-partition problem with no link to the notify path. The notif-worker v3.2.0 rollout at 15:57:45 (#3217) came after the lock holder's transaction had already started (about 15:57:15), and notif-worker logged no errors, so it is an unlikely trigger, though I could not confirm why the reconciler transaction was left open.

The notif-worker v3.2.0 rollout at 15:57:45 is close to the onset of the lock contention. However, the lock holder started about 30s before the deploy and notif-worker shows no errors afterwards, so the link is unconfirmed. Would be the cause if the reconciler's open transaction was introduced by the new build.

input.recommendedAction: Identify and kill the stuck template-svc-reconciler transaction (83136) on notif-db so the row lock is released, then verify notif-db lock waits clear. Investigate why the reconciler left a transaction open for 90s+ (check whether it runs with autocommit off or holds the transaction across a slow external call), and add a lock/idle-transaction timeout. Review whether the notif-worker v3.2.0 rollout (build 86be658) changed the reconciler's behaviour. Consider a circuit breaker or shorter timeout on notification-svc to template-svc so the pool does not saturate. Separately, follow up on the billing-reconciler checksum errors in invoice_archive 2019 partitions and the geo-IP provider 503s, which are out of scope for this incident.
